messages.subject: "grid" integration strategy
parts:
Dear Help,

I would like to inquire whether there were recent changes in the INLA code as regards the "grid" integration strategy?

I get a very large posterior for some parameters (with some quantiles up to 10^85) that I did not get before and this problem does not come up with other integration strategies such as "eb" or "Gaussian". I used "grid" in order to be able to get PIT/CPO.

I could be more precise but I thought that maybe it was due to a general modification of this integration strategy? :o)

Best wishes

Maëlle Salmon.

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "grid" integration strategy
parts:
On Wed, 2015-06-10 at 04:36 -0700, Maëlle Salmon wrote:
> Dear Help,
>
> I would like to inquire whether there were recent changes in the INLA
> code as regards the "grid" integration strategy?
>
> I get a very large posterior for some parameters (with some quantiles
> up to 10^85) that I did not get before and this problem does not come
> up with other integration strategies such as "eb" or "Gaussian". I
> used "grid" in order to be able to get PIT/CPO.
>
> I could be more precise but I thought that maybe it was due to a
> general modification of this integration strategy? :o)

there has been no changes. I think you have run into some numerical
problems, for which errors in the posteriors expose itself in these
quantities. (there is a slight chance that high dependence in the
parameters require argument diff.logdens=20 say or even higher, to
create a box containing all the prob mass for the hyperparameters, and
this is what create the problem).

you do not need grid to compute PIT/CPO. if the Hessian around the mode
(exposed to you as the uncertainty estimate for the hyperparameters) is
ok, then you may want to use int.strategy="eb".


otherwise, I can have a look if you send us data/R-code to rerun it
here.

Best
H
